title: Lambda expressions: syntax, capture and what they replace

videos.script: This course starts where the java course stopped, and its first lesson is about one piece of syntax: the arrow. {{sort}} Here is a list of book titles sorted by length, written the way Java wrote it before 2014. An anonymous class, five lines of ceremony, and one line that matters. {{lambda}} And here is the same sort with a lambda. The one line that mattered is now the whole thing. {{classes}} The compiler agrees that something changed. The anonymous class became a class file of its own. The lambda did not. {{capture}} A lambda can use the variables around it, with one rule the compiler enforces: a local variable it reads must never change. You will see the error, and the reason for it, which comes back when threads arrive in lesson 11. {{close}} Before any of that, the first section checks that your machine has the same Java this course was recorded on.
